image_feature_sections.title: Complexity
image_feature_sections.description: Detail load, structural subdivision, component count, contour count, holes, perimeter load, and angular point count.
image_feature_sections.family_summary: edge density, perimeter/area, quadtree variability, components, contours, holes
image_feature_sections.perception: This family approximates how visually busy or effortful a glyph is to parse. Component and contour counts are pixel-level proxies; human grouping can still differ.
image_feature_sections.low_value: Lower values usually mean a simpler, cleaner symbol with fewer parts, edges, holes, or sharp details.
image_feature_sections.high_value: Higher values usually mean a more intricate symbol that may take more attention to inspect and distinguish.

features.label: Edge density
features.meaning: How much edge/detail structure appears in the icon.
features.category_reason: It belongs in Complexity because edge load reflects visual detail and local structure.
features.evidence: Forsythe et al. used Canny edge density as an automated icon-complexity measure and reported a Spearman correlation of 0.49 with McDougall subjective complexity ratings. Their dual-threshold description also motivates suppressing isolated weak responses. This is the closest measure-level evidence in the local corpus, although the repository implementation is still its own extraction.
features.citation: Forsythe, Sheehy & Sawey, Measuring Icon Complexity: An Automated Analysis, pp. 5-6.

representative_feature.label: Edge density
representative_feature.meaning: How much edge/detail structure appears in the icon.
representative_feature.category_reason: It belongs in Complexity because edge load reflects visual detail and local structure.
representative_feature.evidence: Forsythe et al. used Canny edge density as an automated icon-complexity measure and reported a Spearman correlation of 0.49 with McDougall subjective complexity ratings. Their dual-threshold description also motivates suppressing isolated weak responses. This is the closest measure-level evidence in the local corpus, although the repository implementation is still its own extraction.
representative_feature.citation: Forsythe, Sheehy & Sawey, Measuring Icon Complexity: An Automated Analysis, pp. 5-6.

image_feature_sections.representative_interpretation: Lower values indicate fewer detected edges across the canvas; higher values indicate more connected edge and detail structure.
image_feature_sections.representative_rationale: Selected after the visual audit found that grayscale quadtree variability can reward antialiasing and raster transitions in otherwise simple icons. The current Canny implementation smooths before edge detection and aligns better with the extracted McDougall complexity ratings.
image_feature_sections.representative_evidence: Forsythe et al. describe Canny's dual thresholds as retaining weak edges connected to strong edges while suppressing shading and noise, and report a Spearman correlation of 0.49 with McDougall's subjective complexity ratings.
image_feature_sections.representative_citation: Forsythe, Sheehy & Sawey, Measuring Icon Complexity: An Automated Analysis, pp. 5-6.

image_feature_sections.title: Shape/silhouette
image_feature_sections.description: Silhouette, closure, roundness, rectangularity, and curvature.
image_feature_sections.family_summary: aspect ratio, solidity, closure proxy, circularity/rectangularity, curvature
image_feature_sections.perception: This family captures the overall visible form of a glyph: roundness, box-like form, elongation, closure, curvature, and global silhouette.
image_feature_sections.low_value: Lower values depend on the feature: low circularity means less round, and low closure-proxy values suggest more open or line-like form.
image_feature_sections.high_value: Higher values indicate stronger presence of that specific shape property, such as more circular, more rectangular, or more closed by proxy.

features.label: Enclosure score (v2)
features.meaning: Area enclosed by external foreground contours relative to the active bounding box.
features.category_reason: It belongs in Shape/silhouette because it describes that visual channel.
features.evidence: Fuchs et al. found significant effects of contour variation and showed that contour containment can shift judgments toward geometric-shape similarity. The implemented value approximates enclosed silhouette area; it is not a direct Gestalt-closure score.
features.citation: Fuchs et al., The Influence of Contour on Similarity Perception of Star Glyphs, pp. 2-3 and 6-8.

representative_feature.label: Enclosure score (v2)
representative_feature.meaning: Area enclosed by external foreground contours relative to the active bounding box.
representative_feature.category_reason: It belongs in Shape/silhouette because it describes that visual channel.
representative_feature.evidence: Fuchs et al. found significant effects of contour variation and showed that contour containment can shift judgments toward geometric-shape similarity. The implemented value approximates enclosed silhouette area; it is not a direct Gestalt-closure score.
representative_feature.citation: Fuchs et al., The Influence of Contour on Similarity Perception of Star Glyphs, pp. 2-3 and 6-8.

image_feature_sections.representative_interpretation: Lower values usually mean a thin, open, or spread-out shape. Higher values usually mean a large, compact, or closed shape.
image_feature_sections.representative_rationale: Selected because closure changes whether viewers group a glyph as one coherent shape, making it a direct bridge between silhouette structure and human similarity strategy.
image_feature_sections.representative_evidence: Fuchs et al. found a significant effect of contour variation on accuracy and showed that contour containment shifted judgments toward geometric shape similarity. The implemented value remains a computational proxy, not a direct Gestalt-closure score.
image_feature_sections.representative_citation: Fuchs et al., The Influence of Contour on Similarity Perception of Star Glyphs, pp. 5-8.

image_feature_sections.title: Stroke/structure
image_feature_sections.description: Directional strokes, principal orientation, arrows, arcs, and skeleton graph structure.
image_feature_sections.family_summary: line orientation, principal axis, arrows, arcs, skeleton graph
image_feature_sections.perception: This family captures internal organization: stroke direction, branching, endpoints, arrows, and arcs. It describes visible structure, not exact text or semantic identity.
image_feature_sections.low_value: Lower values usually mean less explicit directionality, fewer skeleton branches/endpoints, or fewer arrows/arcs.
image_feature_sections.high_value: Higher values usually mean stronger directional cues, more branching structure, more endpoints/junctions, or clearer arrow components.

features.label: Principal-axis orientation (v2)
features.meaning: PCA foreground-axis angle over 0-180 degrees; interpret only when orientation confidence is at least 0.20.
features.category_reason: It belongs in Stroke/structure because it describes that visual channel.
features.evidence: Legg et al. report an average human quasi-Hamming distance of 3.0 for orientation, placing it among the more separable primitive groups they tested. PCA axis angle and its confidence rule are project operationalizations, not formulas evaluated in that experiment.
features.citation: Legg et al., Glyph Visualization: A Fail-Safe Design Scheme Based on Quasi-Hamming Distances, pp. 4-6.

representative_feature.label: Principal-axis orientation (v2)
representative_feature.meaning: PCA foreground-axis angle over 0-180 degrees; interpret only when orientation confidence is at least 0.20.
representative_feature.category_reason: It belongs in Stroke/structure because it describes that visual channel.
representative_feature.evidence: Legg et al. report an average human quasi-Hamming distance of 3.0 for orientation, placing it among the more separable primitive groups they tested. PCA axis angle and its confidence rule are project operationalizations, not formulas evaluated in that experiment.
representative_feature.citation: Legg et al., Glyph Visualization: A Fail-Safe Design Scheme Based on Quasi-Hamming Distances, pp. 4-6.

image_feature_sections.representative_interpretation: The value is an axial angle, not an amount: 0° is horizontal, 90° is vertical, and 180° wraps to horizontal. Confidence below 0.20 means undefined.
image_feature_sections.representative_rationale: Selected as the clearest single summary of global stroke direction and because orientation was one of the more separable human-rated visual channels.
image_feature_sections.representative_evidence: The quasi-Hamming study reports an average human perceptual-distance score of 3.0 for orientation, above connection lines (2.8), texture (2.2), color (2.2), size (2.1), and luminance (1.2).
image_feature_sections.representative_citation: Legg et al., Glyph Visualization: A Fail-Safe Design Scheme Based on Quasi-Hamming Distances, p. 5.

image_feature_sections.title: Density/fill
image_feature_sections.description: Foreground amount, bounding-box fill, outline-vs-fill behavior, and stroke thickness.
image_feature_sections.family_summary: foreground amount, bounding-box occupancy, filled/outline proxy, stroke width
image_feature_sections.perception: This family describes whether a glyph reads as sparse line art, a filled silhouette, or a heavy/thick mark.
image_feature_sections.low_value: Lower values usually mean a lighter, thinner, more open, or less filled glyph.
image_feature_sections.high_value: Higher values usually mean a denser, more filled, more visually heavy glyph with thicker strokes or stronger occupancy.

features.label: Solid fill ratio (v2)
features.meaning: Mean foreground survival after erosion at 1%, 2%, and 4% of active-box width/height.
features.category_reason: It belongs in Density/fill because it describes that visual channel.
features.evidence: Fuchs et al. found significant fill-type effects for rotated and scaled similarity choices, showing that filled-versus-outline treatment can alter judgment strategy. They did not establish a general accuracy benefit, and the erosion-survival formula is a project proxy.
features.citation: Fuchs et al., The Influence of Contour on Similarity Perception of Star Glyphs, pp. 2-3 and 6-8.

representative_feature.label: Solid fill ratio (v2)
representative_feature.meaning: Mean foreground survival after erosion at 1%, 2%, and 4% of active-box width/height.
representative_feature.category_reason: It belongs in Density/fill because it describes that visual channel.
representative_feature.evidence: Fuchs et al. found significant fill-type effects for rotated and scaled similarity choices, showing that filled-versus-outline treatment can alter judgment strategy. They did not establish a general accuracy benefit, and the erosion-survival formula is a project proxy.
representative_feature.citation: Fuchs et al., The Influence of Contour on Similarity Perception of Star Glyphs, pp. 2-3 and 6-8.

image_feature_sections.representative_interpretation: Lower values lose foreground quickly under 1%, 2%, and 4% erosion and suggest outlines; higher values retain a solid interior.
image_feature_sections.representative_rationale: Selected because filled-versus-outline treatment directly changes figure-ground structure and has experimental evidence of changing similarity-choice behavior.
image_feature_sections.representative_evidence: Fuchs et al. found significant fill-type effects on rotated and scaled similarity choices. They did not find a general accuracy benefit, so this feature should be interpreted as affecting strategy rather than quality.
image_feature_sections.representative_citation: Fuchs et al., The Influence of Contour on Similarity Perception of Star Glyphs, pp. 6-8.

image_feature_sections.title: Balance/layout
image_feature_sections.description: Centering, symmetry, active bounding-box position/size, and 4x4 foreground grid layout.
image_feature_sections.family_summary: symmetry, centroid, bounding-box position/size, 4x4 grid occupancy
image_feature_sections.perception: This family captures where visual mass sits and whether the glyph feels centered, balanced, symmetric, top-heavy, side-heavy, compact, or spread out. Grid features should be treated as one layout channel when comparing families.
image_feature_sections.low_value: Lower values often mean less offset or less occupancy in a given region; for symmetry scores, lower means less balanced.
image_feature_sections.high_value: Higher values often mean stronger occupancy in a region, larger active extent, more offset for distance features, or stronger balance for symmetry scores.

features.label: Horizontal symmetry (v2)
features.meaning: Left-right Dice-style foreground overlap allowing a two-pixel alignment tolerance.
features.category_reason: It belongs in Balance/layout because it describes that visual channel.
features.evidence: Symmetry is described as a Gestalt organization principle, and the glyph-foundations review reports improved user performance for complexity- and symmetry-optimized star-glyph orderings. The repository's pixel-overlap scores are computational proxies rather than the tested ordering method.
features.citation: Borgo et al., Glyph-based Visualization: Foundations, Design Guidelines, Techniques and Applications, pp. 7-10, 12 and 16.

representative_feature.label: Horizontal symmetry (v2)
representative_feature.meaning: Left-right Dice-style foreground overlap allowing a two-pixel alignment tolerance.
representative_feature.category_reason: It belongs in Balance/layout because it describes that visual channel.
representative_feature.evidence: Symmetry is described as a Gestalt organization principle, and the glyph-foundations review reports improved user performance for complexity- and symmetry-optimized star-glyph orderings. The repository's pixel-overlap scores are computational proxies rather than the tested ordering method.
representative_feature.citation: Borgo et al., Glyph-based Visualization: Foundations, Design Guidelines, Techniques and Applications, pp. 7-10, 12 and 16.

image_feature_sections.representative_interpretation: Lower values indicate weaker left-right correspondence; higher values indicate stronger bilateral Dice overlap with a two-pixel tolerance.
image_feature_sections.representative_rationale: Selected because symmetry is a foundational perceptual-grouping cue, horizontal symmetry has a direct implementation, and symmetry-optimized glyph designs have reported performance benefits.
image_feature_sections.representative_evidence: The glyph-foundations review identifies symmetry as a Gestalt organization principle and reports improved user performance for complexity- and symmetry-optimized star-glyph orderings.
image_feature_sections.representative_citation: Borgo et al., Glyph-based Visualization: Foundations, Design Guidelines, Techniques and Applications, pp. 7, 12 and 16.

image_feature_sections.title: Color/contrast
image_feature_sections.description: Color presence, saturation, colorfulness, foreground-background contrast, hue distribution, and dominant Lab colors.
image_feature_sections.family_summary: monochrome flag, color count, saturation, colorfulness, foreground-background contrast, hue histogram, dominant Lab colors
image_feature_sections.perception: This family captures color channels humans use for quick grouping, salience, and foreground-background separation.
image_feature_sections.low_value: Lower values usually mean less saturation/colorfulness, weaker contrast, or less presence of a given hue bin. For `is_monochrome`, lower means color is present.
image_feature_sections.high_value: Higher values usually mean stronger signal for that specific color feature. For `is_monochrome`, higher means grayscale/monochrome rather than more color.

features.label: Mean saturation (v2)
features.meaning: Mean HSV saturation over corrected foreground pixels.
features.category_reason: It belongs in Color/contrast because it describes that visual channel.
features.evidence: Color, hue, saturation, intensity, and brightness are established glyph channels, with color described as especially strong for pop-out. Legg et al. also obtained human distinguishability ratings for color. These repository summaries operationalize color presence and strength; their exact formulas were not tested by those studies.
features.citation: Borgo et al., Glyph-based Visualization: Foundations, Design Guidelines, Techniques and Applications, pp. 7-10, 12 and 16. Legg et al., Glyph Visualization: A Fail-Safe Design Scheme Based on Quasi-Hamming Distances, pp. 4-6.

representative_feature.label: Mean saturation (v2)
representative_feature.meaning: Mean HSV saturation over corrected foreground pixels.
representative_feature.category_reason: It belongs in Color/contrast because it describes that visual channel.
representative_feature.evidence: Color, hue, saturation, intensity, and brightness are established glyph channels, with color described as especially strong for pop-out. Legg et al. also obtained human distinguishability ratings for color. These repository summaries operationalize color presence and strength; their exact formulas were not tested by those studies.
representative_feature.citation: Borgo et al., Glyph-based Visualization: Foundations, Design Guidelines, Techniques and Applications, pp. 7-10, 12 and 16. Legg et al., Glyph Visualization: A Fail-Safe Design Scheme Based on Quasi-Hamming Distances, pp. 4-6.

image_feature_sections.representative_interpretation: Lower values indicate grayscale or muted corrected foregrounds; higher values indicate more vivid, strongly saturated corrected foreground color.
image_feature_sections.representative_rationale: Selected as a continuous, interpretable color-strength measure that works across the B/W, red, and colored cohorts without privileging one arbitrary hue bin.
image_feature_sections.representative_evidence: The glyph-foundations review describes color as the strongest of the commonly compared pop-out channels. Choosing mean saturation as its operational measure is a project inference; the literature supports the color channel, not this exact formula.
image_feature_sections.representative_citation: Borgo et al., Glyph-based Visualization: Foundations, Design Guidelines, Techniques and Applications, pp. 7-10; Legg et al., Quasi-Hamming Distances, p. 5.

image_feature_sections.title: Texture
image_feature_sections.perception: This family captures internal tonal variation that can affect perceived detail. Artifact-prone local binary pattern bins are excluded from the active visual-family mapping.
image_feature_sections.low_value: Lower values usually mean flatter, more uniform foreground regions with little internal texture or local tonal variation.
image_feature_sections.high_value: Higher values usually mean more internal tonal variation that can make the glyph feel more textured.

features.label: Local texture variation (v2)
features.meaning: Normalized 7x7 local grayscale variation within a two-pixel-eroded foreground interior.
features.category_reason: It belongs in Texture because it describes that visual channel.
features.evidence: Texture produced an average human quasi-Hamming distance of 2.2 in Legg et al., and texture is listed as a glyph visual channel in the foundations review. The normalized local-interior variation formula was not evaluated in those studies and still requires human validation.
features.citation: Legg et al., Glyph Visualization: A Fail-Safe Design Scheme Based on Quasi-Hamming Distances, pp. 4-6. Borgo et al., Glyph-based Visualization: Foundations, Design Guidelines, Techniques and Applications, pp. 7-10, 12 and 16.

representative_feature.label: Local texture variation (v2)
representative_feature.meaning: Normalized 7x7 local grayscale variation within a two-pixel-eroded foreground interior.
representative_feature.category_reason: It belongs in Texture because it describes that visual channel.
representative_feature.evidence: Texture produced an average human quasi-Hamming distance of 2.2 in Legg et al., and texture is listed as a glyph visual channel in the foundations review. The normalized local-interior variation formula was not evaluated in those studies and still requires human validation.
representative_feature.citation: Legg et al., Glyph Visualization: A Fail-Safe Design Scheme Based on Quasi-Hamming Distances, pp. 4-6. Borgo et al., Glyph-based Visualization: Foundations, Design Guidelines, Techniques and Applications, pp. 7-10, 12 and 16.

image_feature_sections.representative_interpretation: Lower values indicate flat interiors; higher values indicate stronger normalized 7x7 grayscale variation inside the eroded foreground, excluding the silhouette edge.
image_feature_sections.representative_rationale: Selected because local interior variation excludes the silhouette boundary and reduces the color/global-tonal leakage found in the legacy entropy proxy.
image_feature_sections.representative_evidence: Texture produced an average human quasi-Hamming perceptual-distance score of 2.2, supporting the construct but not this exact local-variation formula. Human validation remains pending.
image_feature_sections.representative_citation: Legg et al., Glyph Visualization: A Fail-Safe Design Scheme Based on Quasi-Hamming Distances, p. 5; Borgo et al., Glyph-based Visualization, p. 8.
